chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Aban ibn Taghlib said:

I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) the Maghrib prayer in Al-Muzdalifah, so he stood and prayed Maghrib, then he prayed the final 'Isha and did not bow in between. Then I prayed behind him a year later, and when he had prayed Maghrib, he stood and voluntarily prayed four rak'at.
And the boundary of Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram is what is between the two shoulders (or peaks) to Al-Hiyad and to Wadi Muhassir, he narrated that.

key_terms.اَلْمَشْعَرُ اَلْحَرَام: The Sacred Monument (often identified with Mashar Mosque)
key_terms.اَلْمُزْدَلِفَة: A plain near Mecca where pilgrims stay after leaving Mina

ai.seo_question: How did the Imams perform the Maghrib and 'Isha prayers at Al-Muzdalifah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical flexibility in combining Maghrib and 'Isha prayers at Al-Muzdalifah, a key rite of Hajj, by performing them consecutively without an intervening bowing (ruku'), reflecting the scholarly debate on *Jam' Taqdim*. It also provides the precise geographical definition of Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram, extending from the two groves to Wadi Muhassir, which anchors the ritual of standing (wuquf) in a specific physical space. This hadith serves as a primary evidence for the permissibility of shortening the prayer sequence during the Hajj journey, emphasizing ease for pilgrims.
